threat_event: Attacker uses a stolen RMM technician session to push a malicious script to managed customer servers
threat_source: Cybercriminal or state-sponsored group targeting service providers
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Three shared RMM technician accounts; no source-IP restriction on the RMM console; scripts run on any customer without a second approval; RMM logs not in the SIEM
sp800_53_controls: AC-2; AC-6; AC-17; AU-6; SR-6; CM-5
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C AC-2(9), AC-17); C-IT-R05 (12 CFR 53.4(a)); MSA incident notice
existing_controls: Hardware-key MFA on the RMM console; EDR on NOC workstations
treatment_plan: Retire shared accounts; restrict the console to company egress IPs; two-person approval for scripts that target more than one customer; per-customer technician scoping; forward RMM audit logs to the SIEM with alerting (see P08)

threat_event: Theft of control plane service credentials lets an attacker delete, snapshot, or copy any customer VM
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Control plane holds long-lived API credentials to all hypervisor managers; production and non-production share one cloud account; secrets readable by build runners
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-02; SYS-04; SYS-06; all customer VMs (BP-01, BP-02)
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C IA-5, SC-12, AC-6)
existing_controls: Secrets in the cloud provider's secrets manager; hardware-key MFA for engineers
treatment_plan: Separate production into its own cloud account; short-lived, scoped credentials to hypervisor managers; remove secret read access from build runners; alert on bulk snapshot or delete actions

threat_event: Attacker who reaches the management network takes over hypervisor managers or host BMCs
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Local accounts and shared root credentials; no MFA at the hypervisor and BMC layer; management network reachable from the NOC network
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C IA-2(1), AC-2(9), SC-7)
existing_controls: Bastion host with MFA; password vault for root credentials
treatment_plan: Federate hypervisor managers to the workforce IdP with MFA; named admin accounts; BMCs reachable only from the bastion; vault checkout with approval and rotation after use

threat_event: Destructive or ransomware attack deletes the control plane and its backups
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Backups in the same account and region as production; not immutable; same admin roles can delete both
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C CP-9, CP-6)
existing_controls: Nightly database backups; hardware-key MFA for cloud administrators
treatment_plan: Separate backup account with immutable retention in a second region; separate backup administrator role; hourly database snapshots to meet the 1-hour RPO

threat_event: Control plane cannot be restored within the 4-hour RTO after a failure
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Backups never restore-tested; no recovery runbook; RPO 24 hours against a 1-hour target
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C CP-4, CP-10)
existing_controls: Nightly backups; infrastructure-as-code for the cloud tenant
treatment_plan: Write the control plane recovery runbook; quarterly restore tests with timing; first test 2026-11-15

threat_event: Exploitation of an unpatched hypervisor or BMC vulnerability
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One cluster one major release behind; BMC firmware not patched on a schedule; no authenticated internal scanning
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C RA-5, SI-2; FedRAMP VDR rules)
existing_controls: Management network not internet-facing; quarterly external scans
treatment_plan: Monthly authenticated scans of hypervisors, BMCs, and network devices; upgrade the lagging cluster; quarterly BMC firmware cycle; track known exploited vulnerabilities against the CISA catalog

threat_event: Credential stuffing takes over a customer portal account and the attacker controls that customer's VMs and DNS
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Customer MFA optional (38% of customer administrators enrolled); no bot or credential-stuffing protection
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C IA-8, AC-7); MSA
existing_controls: Account lockout after 10 failures; TLS
treatment_plan: Require MFA for customer administrator roles; offer phishing-resistant options; breached-password check; login anomaly alerts

threat_event: Hypervisor flaw allows a VM to reach another tenant's memory or storage
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Shared hypervisor clusters; one cluster behind on releases
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C SC-39)
existing_controls: Hypervisor vendor isolation features enabled; tenant network isolation
treatment_plan: Covered by the R-006 patch program; vendor advisory subscription (SI-5)

threat_event: Privileged administrator views or copies customer VM data without a business need
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No access reviews; hypervisor console and snapshot actions not logged centrally; no two-person rule for snapshot export
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C AC-6, AU-6); MSA confidentiality clause
existing_controls: Background checks; confidentiality agreements
treatment_plan: Forward hypervisor audit logs to the SIEM; alert on console and snapshot export; quarterly access reviews; ticket reference required for console access

threat_event: Former employee uses access that was not removed promptly
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Access removal takes up to 3 business days; RMM and hypervisor local accounts removed by hand
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C PS-4, AC-2(3))
existing_controls: HR emails IT at termination; SSO disable removes most SaaS access
treatment_plan: Same-day disable from the HR ticket; local account checklist for RMM, hypervisor, and BMC; monthly reconciliation

threat_event: Malicious code inserted into the CI/CD pipeline or a VM template that customers deploy
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Template signing key stored as a pipeline secret; hotfixes can bypass review; build runners share the production account
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C SA-10, SI-7)
existing_controls: Pull-request review with one approver for normal changes
treatment_plan: Move the signing key to a cloud HSM with signing-only access; block review bypass; isolated build account; verify template signatures at deploy

threat_event: Volumetric DDoS against DNS and edge network
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Shared edge for all customers
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C SC-5); MSA SLA
existing_controls: DDoS scrubbing service; two carriers per site; secondary DNS
treatment_plan: Annual scrubbing failover test; document the runbook in P08 companion procedures

threat_event: Hijack of the company's own domains through registrar account compromise
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Registrar account uses a shared mailbox for recovery
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C SC-20)
existing_controls: Registrar lock; hardware-key MFA on the registrar account
treatment_plan: Move recovery email to a restricted alias; confirm registry lock

threat_event: Phishing takes over a workforce SSO account
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Phishing-resistant keys in place; residual risk from session token theft
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C IA-2(1))
existing_controls: Hardware security keys for all staff; EDR
treatment_plan: Accepted by the COO: residual risk Low

threat_event: An intrusion goes undetected because key logs are not collected or kept
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Hypervisor, BMC, network, and RMM logs not in the SIEM; 90-day retention
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C AU-2, AU-6, AU-11, SI-4)
existing_controls: SIEM with IdP, cloud tenant, and EDR logs
treatment_plan: Onboard the missing log sources; 1-year retention; weekly review of admin activity

threat_event: AI triage closes or down-ranks a true-positive alert
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: AI auto-close enabled since April 2026 with no sampling or recall measurement
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C SI-4)
existing_controls: Analyst reviews High and Critical alerts
treatment_plan: Disable auto-close for privileged-access and RMM alerts; weekly sample of auto-closed alerts (see P10)

threat_event: Untested change to data center network or hypervisors causes a wide outage
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No change records or approval step for data center changes; hotfix bypass for control plane
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C CM-3, CM-4)
existing_controls: Maintenance windows announced on the status page
treatment_plan: Lightweight change process in the ticketing system: risk rating, peer approval, rollback plan; weekly change review

threat_event: Hurricane or regional disaster takes DC-1 offline for days
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Only about 30% of customer VMs replicate to DC-2; no documented site failover plan
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C CP-6, CP-7); MSA SLA
existing_controls: Colocation facility built to a high wind rating with generators; DC-2 out of state
treatment_plan: Site failover plan and annual exercise; offer discounted replication before hurricane season; state backup responsibility in renewals

threat_event: Power or cooling failure at a colocation facility
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Dependence on provider facilities
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C PE-11, PE-14)
existing_controls: Provider UPS, generators, and cooling redundancy per its SOC 2 report
treatment_plan: Annual review of colocation SOC 2 reports (P09)

threat_event: Storage array firmware defect corrupts customer volumes
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Firmware updates applied without staging
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C CM-3)
existing_controls: Vendor support contract; array snapshots
treatment_plan: Stage firmware on the DC-2 array first; include in change process (R-017)

threat_event: Upstream carrier outage at one site
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: None significant; two carriers per site
regulatory_driver: MSA SLA
existing_controls: Two carriers per site with automatic failover
treatment_plan: Accepted by the COO: residual risk Low

threat_event: Bank customers are not notified within the bank service provider rule after a 4-hour disruption
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No notification procedure; no current list of bank-designated points of contact
existing_controls: NOC status page
treatment_plan: Collect and verify bank-designated contacts; add the 4-hour check to the runbook (P08); quarterly contact verification

threat_event: The FedRAMP Rev5 application window closes, or the sponsor withdraws, before the company is ready
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: New Rev5 applications close 2027-06-11; Rev5 Agency Certification needs the agency's ATO first; readiness gaps are broad (P03)
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (FedRAMP Consolidated Rules for 2026: FRC-APS-ATO; Rev5 application end date)
existing_controls: Contracted FedRAMP advisor; letter of interest from the agency
treatment_plan: Decision gate with the sponsor by 2026-12-31; fund readiness sprints; if the gate is missed, keep the Class C control work as the commercial baseline and revisit FedRAMP options in 2027

threat_event: Customer data recovered from a failed drive that leaves the data center
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: VM volumes not encrypted by default; drive return process not documented
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C MP-6, SC-28(1))
existing_controls: Self-encrypting drives; failed drives kept on site
treatment_plan: Document cryptographic erase and destruction with certificates; default volume encryption (R-031)

threat_event: Breach at the RMM or SIEM vendor exposes the company's customers
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No review of the RMM vendor's SOC 2 report; no contract security terms
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C SR-6, SA-9); MSA
existing_controls: Vendor MFA; hardware keys
treatment_plan: Vendor tiering; annual SOC 2 review for critical vendors; incident notice terms in contracts

threat_event: Attacker uses a manufacturer default BMC account to take over hosts
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Default administrator account enabled on 2 BMCs at DC-2 (found in P07 testing)
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: Rev5 Class C IA-5, CM-6)
existing_controls: BMCs on the management network
treatment_plan: Disable default accounts on all BMCs; add a default-credential check to monthly scans

threat_event: A customer VM is used for phishing or botnet activity and company IP ranges are blocklisted
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Self-service provisioning with limited abuse checks
regulatory_driver: MSA acceptable use terms
existing_controls: Abuse mailbox; acceptable use policy in the MSA
treatment_plan: Outbound spam and scan detection; abuse handling procedure with 24-hour response

threat_event: Support staff share one customer's snapshot or data with the wrong tenant
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Manual snapshot sharing through the hypervisor manager
regulatory_driver: MSA confidentiality clause
existing_controls: Ticket-based requests
treatment_plan: Snapshot sharing only through the portal workflow; role-based training

threat_event: The company misses customer notice duties after a breach of customer data
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No written incident response plan; notice duties in the MSA and Fla. Stat. 501.171(6) not mapped
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171(6); MSA 72-hour notice
existing_controls: Ad hoc NOC communication
treatment_plan: Adopt POL-03 and the P08 runbook with notice clocks; tabletop exercise

threat_event: Security work stalls because one part-time person holds all security duties
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: IT Manager is part-time Information Security Officer; no dedicated security engineer
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (readiness target: FedRAMP Assurance rulesets such as IEC, VDR, and CCM need a staffed security function)
existing_controls: FedRAMP advisor on contract
treatment_plan: Hire a security engineer (approved for 2027 Q1); document procedures so duties can be shared

threat_event: Encryption cannot be shown to use validated modules, forcing rework before any agency use
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Cryptographic modules undocumented; VM volumes not encrypted by default
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R01 (FedRAMP CMU-CSO-CMD; Rev5 Class C SC-13, SC-28(1))
existing_controls: TLS 1.2+; self-encrypting drives
treatment_plan: Inventory cryptographic modules and validation status; default encryption for new volumes

threat_event: Lost or stolen laptop
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Laptops travel to customer sites and data centers
regulatory_driver: MSA confidentiality clause
existing_controls: Full-disk encryption; EDR; hardware keys; remote wipe
treatment_plan: Accepted by the COO: residual risk Low
